95.q: An aircraft approaching an NDB on heading 240°, ADF reads 000°. The aircraft maintains heading but drifts to the left. The ADF reading will be:

o: an apparent turn to the North
ground radio aid used to measure the true altitude of the aircraft
self-contained on-board aid used to measure the true height of the aircraft
self-contained on-board aid used to measure the true altitude of the aircraft

99.q: Aeroplane loading: A) must be performed under the supervision of qualified personnel; B) must be consistent with the data used for calculating the mass and balance; C) must comply with compartment dimension limitations; D) must comply with the maximum load per running metre; E) must comply with the maximum mass per cargo compartment.
o: A, B, C, D and E

ex.5: Sunset (LMT) 1941 observed at 2113 UTC: the observer is 92 min of time west = 23° W.
ex.10: The antipode has the opposite latitude and the longitude 180° away: 180° − 2° 16.5' = 177° 43.5' W.
ex.14: In the northern hemisphere the compass lags turning onto north, so roll out early: about 350° when turning right onto 360°.
ex.18: Wind 65° off the left of the nose: drift ≈ asin(30 × sin 65° / 270) ≈ 6° right; GS ≈ 270 − 30 cos 65° ≈ 259 kt.
ex.19: Adding 135 kt on 278° and the wind (from 140°, blowing towards 320°) at 20 kt gives a track of about 284° and a GS of about 150 kt.
ex.20: TH = 215 + 15 = 230°, TT = 225°, GS = 64 NM in 12 min = 320 kt. Ground vector − air vector gives a wind of about 264°/50 kt.
ex.21: For a given course, drift is greatest when the wind blows at 90° to it: 095 + 90 = 185°.
ex.33: TOM limited by MLM + trip = 75 000 kg. Traffic = 75 000 − 9800 − 48 000 = 17 200 kg.
ex.34: TOM limits: MTOM 52 400; MLM + trip 50 700; MZFM + fuel 51 100 → 50 700. Traffic = 50 700 − 8000 − 29 800 = 12 900 kg.
ex.35: Fuel = 20 100 × 0.79 = 15 879 kg, so take-off fuel 15 629 kg. Lowest TOM limit is MLM + trip = 58 900 + 5990 = 64 890 kg. Traffic = 64 890 − 15 629 − 34 930 = 14 331 kg.
ex.51: Departure = Δlong × cos lat: 1' × cos 60° = 0.5 NM.
ex.75: With 090 selected and TO showing, the aircraft is west of the station. Needle right means the 270 radial is to the right, so the aircraft is north of it: about 275.
ex.78: OBS 330 with the aircraft on radial 120 gives TO. Looking along 330°, the 150 radial (the selected inbound line) is to the left of the aircraft, so fly left.
ex.79: On radial 090 and heading roughly back towards the station, select 270 for a centred needle with TO.
ex.80: More 90 Hz on the localiser means the aircraft is left of the centre-line (fly right); more 90 Hz on the glide path means it is above (fly down).
ex.86: 23 000 ft; 80 NM at 240 kt = 20 min → 1150 ft/min.
ex.87: 15 × 6000 × 3/60 = 4500 ft, plus the 50 ft threshold crossing height = 4550 ft.
ex.89: A 3° path is about 300 ft per NM: 1500 / 300 = 5 NM.
ex.90: Conversion angle = ½ × d.long × sin mean lat, so it grows with both latitude and d.long.
ex.95: Drifting left puts the beacon to the right of the nose, so the relative bearing becomes slightly more than 000°.
